PIT Lab · real mutation testing, running in your browser

Test your tests: break the code on purpose.

PIT changes the compiled code in small ways ("mutants"), then re-runs the unit tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is killed. If every test still passes, the mutant survived, which means the suite would miss that bug. Everything below runs for real: mutants are generated from the rule source, compiled and executed against the JUnit suite. Add tests and watch the score change.

01 · COVERAGEFind covering tests

PIT first measures which tests execute each line, so it only runs the tests that can reach a mutant.

02 · MUTATEGenerate mutants

Mutators rewrite bytecode: < to <=, + to −, return values to 0/""/true…

03 · EXECUTERun tests per mutant

Each mutant is loaded in a minion JVM. The first failing test kills it and PIT moves on.

04 · REPORTMutation score

Killed ÷ total. CI fails the build if it is below mutationThreshold.
